title: Coherence of the standard Proj chart rings
statement:
For positive-degree homogeneous $f,g,h$, localization induces canonical
equivalences between the restrictions of $(R_{(f)})_0$ and
$(R_{(g)})_0$ to the overlap indexed by $fg$. These equivalences are the
identity for $f=g$, are inverse under exchange of $f$ and $g$, and satisfy
the cocycle equality on the triple localization indexed by $fgh$.

proof.text: Write $R=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}R_n$, $f\in R_d$, $g\in R_e$, $h\in R_k$ with $d,e,k>0$, and $A_f=R_{(f),0}$. Put $t_{fg}=g^d/f^e\in A_f$ and $B_f^g=(A_f)_{t_{fg}}$. These are the restrictions on the overlap: the cited basic-open statement identifies it in the f chart as the principal open of $t_{fg}$. Apply the ring case $M=R$ of the graded restriction theorem, extending the grading of R by zero in negative degrees. Use the relation $fg=g\cdot f$ (relation exponent 1, homogeneous multiplier g). Its ring restriction map $r_{f,fg}:A_f\to A_{fg}$ sends $x/f^m$ to $xg^m/(fg)^m$. The theorem's localizing element is $(fg)^d/f^{d+e}=g^d/f^e=t_{fg}$: the equality is cancellation of the unit f in the ordinary localization at f, hence equality in its degree-zero subring. Clause (iii) therefore gives a ring isomorphism $E_f^g:B_f^g\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{fg}$ with $E_f^g(q/t_{fg}^n)=r_{f,fg}(q)r_{f,fg}(t_{fg})^{-n}$. Exchange f and g to obtain $E_g^f:B_g^f\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{fg}$, using the literal equality $gf=fg$. No assertion about a map $A_f\to A_g$ before restricting is needed.

source.place: Tag 01M4, label lemma-standard-open, (1)(c),(d),(e); apply to f and fg, then fg and fgh

proof.text: Define the transition $\alpha_{fg}=(E_g^f)^{-1}\circ E_f^g:B_f^g\xrightarrow{\sim}B_g^f$. Both comparisons are induced by the same homogeneous fractions in $R_{fg}$, so this is the canonical localization-induced equivalence. In particular its characterization is $E_g^f\alpha_{fg}=E_f^g$. When $f=g$, the two comparisons are the same map, and $\alpha_{ff}=(E_f^f)^{-1}E_f^f=\mathrm{id}$. Here $t_{ff}=f^d/f^d=1$, so restricting the self-overlap also canonically gives $A_f$. Under exchange, $\alpha_{gf}=(E_f^g)^{-1}E_g^f=\alpha_{fg}^{-1}$, by cancellation of inverse ring isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 01M4, label lemma-standard-open, (1)(c),(d),(e); apply to f and fg, then fg and fgh

proof.text: For the triple overlap put $u_f=(gh)^d/f^{e+k}=t_{fg}t_{fh}$ and $T_f=(A_f)_{u_f}$, with cyclic definitions $T_g,T_h$. The ring case of clause (iii) for the relation $fgh=(gh)f$ supplies $E_f:T_f\xrightarrow{\sim}C$, where $C=A_{fgh}$; similarly obtain $E_g,E_h$. These are the triple restrictions: inverting a product of two elements is equivalent to inverting both. Explicitly if ab is a unit then $b(ab)^{-1}$ is an inverse of a and $a(ab)^{-1}$ is an inverse of b; conversely the product of two units is a unit. The universal property supplies the maps to and from successive localizations, and its uniqueness makes the composites identities. This verifies the iterated-restriction identification without assuming any of f,g,h are non-zero-divisors.

source.place: Tag 01M4, label lemma-standard-open, (1)(c),(d),(e); apply to f and fg, then fg and fgh

proof.text: There is a canonical restriction $j_f^g:B_f^g\to T_f$, sending $q/t_{fg}^n$ to $(q/1)(t_{fg}/1)^{-n}$; it exists since $t_{fg}/1$ is a unit by the product calculation. Likewise $j_g^f$. Let $r_{fg,fgh}:A_{fg}\to C$ be the ring restriction for $fgh=h(fg)$. On a generator $q=x/f^m\in A_f$, the composite restriction has value $xg^mh^m/(fgh)^m$, equal to the direct restriction $x(gh)^m/(fgh)^m$. Thus $r_{fg,fgh}r_{f,fg}=r_{f,fgh}$. The extension formulas of clause (iii), followed by uniqueness in the localization universal property, give $E_fj_f^g=r_{fg,fgh}E_f^g$; the same holds for g. Each equality is checked on all q/1; inverses of the localizing element then force equality on q/t^n. Consequently $\beta_{fg}=E_g^{-1}E_f:T_f\xrightarrow{\sim}T_g$ satisfies $\beta_{fg}j_f^g=j_g^f\alpha_{fg}$. It is the restriction of $\alpha_{fg}$: indeed it carries the image of $t_{fh}$ to a unit, because its product with the already invertible image of $t_{fg}$ is the unit $u_f$, and the iterated-localization uniqueness just proved makes this extension unique. Repeat for the pairs g,h and f,h.

source.place: Tag 01M4, label lemma-standard-open, (1)(c),(d),(e); apply to f and fg, then fg and fgh

proof.text: All triple transitions now have the common target C in their definitions. For $z\in T_f$, compute $\beta_{gh}(\beta_{fg}(z))=E_h^{-1}(E_g(E_g^{-1}(E_f(z))))=E_h^{-1}(E_f(z))=\beta_{fh}(z)$. Equality on every z proves $\beta_{gh}\circ\beta_{fg}=\beta_{fh}$. By the preceding commuting squares these are precisely the restrictions of the original double-overlap transitions, so this is the claimed cocycle on the localization indexed by fgh.

split_report.summary: Made the overlap restrictions explicit, reused the general graded-module-away restriction theorem in its ring case, and proved identity, inverse, and triple cocycle by comparisons with a common homogeneous localization. No new nodes: the prospective product-localization fact is already a special case of an existing node.

lean.statement:
theorem Away.overlapEquiv_cocycle {d e e' : ι} {f g h z : A} (hf : f ∈ 𝒜 d) (hg : g ∈ 𝒜 e)
    (hh : h ∈ 𝒜 e') (hz : z = f * g * h) :
    (awayMap 𝒜 hh (hz.trans (by ring) : z = g * f * h)).comp
        (Away.overlapEquiv 𝒜 f g).toRingHom = awayMap 𝒜 hh hz ∧
      (awayMap 𝒜 hf (hz.trans (by ring) : z = h * g * f)).comp
        (Away.overlapEquiv 𝒜 g h).toRingHom =
          awayMap 𝒜 hf (hz.trans (by ring) : z = g * h * f) ∧
      (awayMap 𝒜 hg (hz.trans (by ring) : z = h * f * g)).comp
        (Away.overlapEquiv 𝒜 f h).toRingHom =
          awayMap 𝒜 hg (hz.trans (by ring) : z = f * h * g)
lean.note: Existing published chart-coherence family, read using scompile.py --source (the local slopmaster2 checkout predates it). The overlap rings are represented by Away at fg and gf; Mathlib Away.isLocalization_mul identifies these with the two restricted chart rings. overlapEquiv and the two awayMap compatibility lemmas supply the canonical equivalence; self and symm supply identity and inverse; overlapEquiv_cocycle identifies all three further restrictions with the common Away ring at fgh. Specialize the general grading to ℕ and the homogeneous degrees to positive ones.

blueprint_update.statement:
For positive-degree homogeneous $f,g,h$, localization induces canonical
equivalences between the restrictions of $(R_{(f)})_0$ and
$(R_{(g)})_0$ to the overlap indexed by $fg$. These equivalences are the
identity for $f=g$, are inverse under exchange of $f$ and $g$, and satisfy
the cocycle equality on the triple localization indexed by $fgh$.

proof.text:
Use the canonical maps between the homogeneous localizations at $f$, $g$,
and $fg$. On a representative $x/f^m$ each map sends the fraction to its
image in the localization at $fg$; the localization relation proves
independence of representatives. The identity, inverse, and triple
cocycle equations follow because both sides are the same map into the
localization at $fgh$. These are the compatibilities used by the verified
declarations `Proj.basicOpenIsoSpec` and
`Proj.affineOpenCover`.
